<!-- pr-reviewer: 9ea79086c6aff79f22eb71a751a8a09bcebbcbfa -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

Review of head `9ea79086c` (the rework of the seven findings), trial-merged with `origin/side/path-kernel` `d1feeb12d` (already an ancestor: no conflicts, no hand edits). This is a SAFETY-tier review: the switch sits on the generation path.

## What looks good

- The switch is one rule: `camcraft_motion::pathkernel::{PLANNER_ENV, PlannerEngine, engine_from_switch}` parsed once (`OnceLock`) in `planner_engine()`; `check_engine(kind, engine)` runs in `run_job` before every arm; the 16 phase-1 kinds are refused by name under `new`; a bad value gives the old planner and one diagnostic. The default arms are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- The 17 baseline goldens of `9c69f004a` are additions copied unchanged: all 17 files are byte-for-byte equal to the baseline commit (verified with `cmp`, line and line ending). No recorded program moves.
- All seven findings are closed by `9ea79086c`, one rule per class, and the tests use the public API in the new suite `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws.rs` (see the mapping below).
- `cl_text_round_trips_every_golden` is not weaker: the CL text of each golden still round-trips, and the tail is asserted to hold only `; note:` / `; warning:` lines. A plain golden (no annotation) is checked exactly as before.
- The dependency edges match the approved decision `docs/decisions/4024-path-kernel-design.md` ("Dependency decision"): `camcraft-pathkernel -> camcraft-geometry` (Point2, Region, the loop and polyline types - the record says K1 fixes the exact list; this step imports `Loop, Point2, Region`), `camcraft-motion -> camcraft-pathkernel` (re-export only; the record lists Recipe/plan_level/region/etc. for K1 - this step carries none). The app gets the crate through motion (`camcraft_app::pathkernel`); there is no direct app edge. Process change: yes is present and `PROCESS_VERSION` is untouched.

## Results merged with side/path-kernel (d1feeb12d)

Built locally on the review worktree `.claude/worktrees/cc-pr4123-review`, 6 jobs. Two builds of other sessions were already on the host; this review's build was the third.

- `cargo test -p camcraft-pathkernel`: 33 laws tests + unit tests, all pass (0 failed).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-pathkernel -p camcraft-motion --all-targets` (`-D warnings` on the lint set): both pass, 0 warnings.
- `cargo test -p xtask -- the_gate_lists_name_every_workspace_crate a_pathkernel_change_plans_its_suites_and_the_mapped_app_suite reach_follows_the_crate_dependencies`: 3 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-cl --test headless_bin -- cl_text_round_trips_every_golden`: 1 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test offset_pass_start -- switch_default_passes_each_phase1_kind_to_the_old_planner switch_new_refuses_a_kind_it_does_not_plan_yet`: 2 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test pass_start_levels -- shared_planner` (the #3750 baseline pins, cherry-picked): 3 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: 43 passed, 4 ignored, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog_adaptive`: 1 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog_edge_work`: 1 passed, 0 failed.
- The full `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/side/path-kernel` was NOT run locally: it becomes a batch (1222 steps, ~60 min at this machine's rate) and the host carried two other builds. The author reports 1222 steps, 0 failed, on this head (gate logs `gate-logs/`); the quick-plan dry-run confirms the plan shape (1222 steps). The targeted equivalents above cover the PR's own suites.
- The light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`): all 6 steps pass: `light build (release --no-run)` (380s), `motion light: lib` (355s, 8 ignored tests run), `motion light: adaptive_troch_island` (47s), `motion light: adaptive_troch_neck` (18s), `motion light: adaptive_troch_parallel` (12s), `app light: pocket_pass_start` (3s) - 6 steps, 0 failed, wall 13.6 min, log dir `gate-logs/light-20261126-092653`.

## Findings to commit mapping

- Finding 1 (curve topology / arc identity): `9ea79086c` (`Curve::same_cut`: same index, family, closure and circle within tolerance; a closed curve is a cyclic shift or reversal of the input; an open curve is the input or its reverse, `guide.rs:280` (`Curve::same_cut`); the start point must be the first point of the first curve, `order.rs:59` (`OrderedSet::new`)). Closed by the `order` suite.
- Finding 2 (step transitions): `9ea79086c` (`Plan::new`, the transition table: a cut consumes the readiness, each cut needs its own entry or stay-down link, `plan.rs:83-95`). Closed by the `plan` suite.
- Finding 3 (construction paths): `9ea79086c` (one rule: valid by construction; fields are private, enum variants hold validated newtypes, `Recipe` checks its own pair). Closed by the `construction` suite.
- Finding 4 (proof place binding): `9ea79086c` (`Proof` names its place; each descent move stays in it; a pre-drilled proof must name one of the holes, `entry.rs:161`). Closed by the `entry` suite.
- Finding 5 (overload records): `9ea79086c` (`Controlled::new`: limit in (0, 1]; each reading over the limit named exactly once; each record agrees with a reading, `load.rs:192`). Closed by the `load` suite.
- Finding 6 (canonical set ties): `9ea79086c` (`Curve::canonical` + the total order in `GuideSet`: index, family, open before closed, the canonical point sequence, the circle; equal lowest points give one start). Closed by the `guide` suite.
- Finding 7 (golden inventory): not a code commit. The PR body now carries the heading `Goldens moved` with all 17 files as additions copied unchanged from `9c69f004a`; the review instructions ask for that list, and it is present and accurate.

## Not run / not exercised

- The full quick gate and the full batch tier (host load; see above). The author reports 1222 steps, 0 failed on `9ea79086c`.
- The heavy pins `switch_default_is_the_old_planner` and `fig8_offset_rings_unchanged_by_the_shared_planner` (both `#[ignore]`d, release lane) were NOT run by this review; the author reports them green in release (107.6 s). This is not a blocker: the PR is P2, not P1, under the safety floor, and the cherry-picked #3750 goldens are checked byte-for-byte against the baseline commit.
- `cl_text_round_trips_every_golden` covers the goldens; it does not cover the 17 new goldens byte-for-byte beyond what the app `shared_planner` test already compares.

## Questions

- None blocking. The `docs/decisions/4055-pathkernel-skeleton.md` record (items 12 to 17) documents each rule and the tests that pin it; nothing is missing for the review's scope.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
